relationships.subject: Galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Galcanezumab is a humanized IgG4 mAb that binds to both the α and β forms of CGRP.[40]

relationships.subject: Erenumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Erenumab, a CGRP receptor blocker, is a humanized IgG2 mAb that has been found to have an early-onset efficacy.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: During activation of the TVS, CGRP leads to neurogenic inflammation in the meningeal vasculature and mast cell degranulation resulting in peripheral sensitization

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: the release of CGRP activates the satellite glia cells, which release proinflammatory cytokines and results in a positive feedback loop.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: CGRP increases purinergic P2X3 gene expression in nociceptive TG neurons, furthering CGRP release.

key_findings: Narrative review: CGRP drives trigeminovascular neurogenic inflammation and sensitization; four anti-CGRP mAbs (erenumab to receptor; eptinezumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab to ligand) are approved.
About 48-62% of patients achieve >50% MMD reduction with these mAbs.
